McLaren.summary: McLaren’s new front‑corner package features a larger, high‑flow brake duct tailored to this circuit’s demands, keeping the front brakes cooler under the heavy braking zones. The extra cooling means the driver can push harder into corners without worrying about brake fade, giving the team a better chance to attack and defend throughout the weekend.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has re‑shaped the front wing, redistributing the surface area across its three panels and moving to a two‑piece layout, while also tweaking the endplates, footplate and dive‑plane angle to keep the airflow tighter. The result should be cleaner air to the car’s floor and rear, giving a little extra grip in the corners and a smoother ride on the straights. In short, it’s a subtle front‑end clean‑up aimed at shaving off tenths of a second and keeping the car stable over the weekend’s bumpy tracks.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull’s new front wing now features a reshaped end plate and flap, giving the car better bite in the corners and more stable grip as it tackles the circuit’s high‑speed bends. At the rear, a larger exit duct has been added to the wheel‑body area, helping to keep the car cooler and more reliable over a full race distance. Together, these tweaks should translate into sharper handling and fewer overheating issues, giving the team a stronger chance to fight for podium positions this weekend.
